_source: Synthesized 2026-08-09 by the creative-research-curate workflow (5 high-effort agents: UGC, promo, product-shot, commercial, ad-creative). External best-practice research — confidence 'documented' unless it restates a measured house law. Promote to 'measured' only after an A/B on our own endpoint.

ugc:hook-rate-35pct-gates-scale.claim: A UGC ad's 3-second hook rate (3s views / impressions) must clear ~35% before scaling spend; below that the hook is broken and nothing downstream matters. It is the primary kill/keep metric, not CTR or CVR.
ugc:hook-rate-35pct-gates-scale.evidence: 2026 UGC playbooks converge on >35% 3s hook-rate as the scale threshold and state the first 1-3s decides whether the rest is watched (gethookd, vidovo, koro).
ugc:hook-rate-35pct-gates-scale.counterexamples: Threshold is platform- and price-point-dependent and NOT measured on our own endpoint; a high-consideration product may scale on a lower hook rate with strong hold.

ugc:failed-attempts-beat-buys-believabil.claim: Insert an explicit 'failed attempts' beat ('I tried X and Y and nothing worked...') between problem and discovery. Without it the arc reads too clean and less believable; with it the testimonial reads as lived experience.
ugc:failed-attempts-beat-buys-believabil.evidence: 2026 script-structure guides prescribe hook -> problem -> failed attempts -> discovery -> result -> soft CTA and call the failed-attempts beat the specific realism lever (shortgenius, retiplex, admove).
ugc:failed-attempts-beat-buys-believabil.counterexamples: Adds length; in a 5-10s cut there may be no room, so it is a 20s+ structural law, not a universal one. Not A/B-tested on our corpus.
ugc:failed-attempts-beat-buys-believabil.source: shortgenius.com script-templates-2026; retiplex.com ugc-ad-script-guide; admove.ai how-to-create-ugc-ads

ugc:soft-cta-beats-hard-cta.claim: Close on a recommendation-style soft CTA ('check it out if you're dealing with the same thing'), never an imperative 'Buy now'. A hard CTA breaks the peer-to-peer authenticity the rest of the ad built and signals 'ad'.
ugc:soft-cta-beats-hard-cta.evidence: Multiple 2026 sources state 'soft beats hard' and that aggressive CTAs collapse the authenticity UGC depends on (retiplex, inbeat, thebrief).
ugc:soft-cta-beats-hard-cta.counterexamples: Direct-response accounts with a promo/deadline sometimes need an explicit offer CTA; the softness trades measured urgency for perceived authenticity.
ugc:soft-cta-beats-hard-cta.source: retiplex.com ugc-ad-script-guide; inbeat.agency tiktok-ugc; thebrief.ai ugc-video-ads-guide

ugc:polish-is-inversely-correlated-with-.claim: In the UGC lane, higher production polish LOWERS performance — studio lighting, retouched skin, and a colour grade signal 'advertising' and get down-ranked by both viewers and the feed algorithm. Cap the niceness; native-looking wins.
ugc:polish-is-inversely-correlated-with-.evidence: 2026 sources: UGC is ~22% more effective than brand-made video, over-polished content underperforms, platforms boost organic-looking content; corroborated by our house law that skin texture (not grade) carries realism (adconvert, theshortmedia, bambassadors).
ugc:polish-is-inversely-correlated-with-.counterexamples: Some hybrid 'premium UGC' works for luxury/beauty; the law is lane-scoped to organic testimonial, not to all social video. Not measured on our endpoint.
ugc:polish-is-inversely-correlated-with-.source: adconvert.org ugc-style-ai-ads; theshortmedia.com why-ugc-outperform-2025; bambassadors.com native-ugc

ugc:rotate-20-to-50-hooks-against-one-bo.claim: Fight creative fatigue by testing 20-50 distinct hook openers against the same tested body, rather than re-rolling whole ads or one hook. The hook is the highest-variance, fastest-fatiguing element, so hook volume is the account-level lever.
ugc:rotate-20-to-50-hooks-against-one-bo.evidence: 2026 UGC guidance states relying on a single hook burns budget and that top brands now test 20-50 hook variations programmatically (pixis, influee).
ugc:rotate-20-to-50-hooks-against-one-bo.counterexamples: Requires a body that is already a proven winner; spraying hooks on a weak body just fails faster. Volume claim is an industry norm, not measured here.

static-ad:master-at-4x5-1080x1350-for-fe.claim: Build the Meta feed static at 4:5 (1080x1350px) as the master, then export 9:16 (1080x1920) for Stories/Reels and 1:1 (1080x1080) for square-safe placements. 4:5 occupies the most vertical mobile screen and measurably out-CTRs 1:1 and 16:9; never send 16:9 or 2:1 landscape to feed.
static-ad:master-at-4x5-1080x1350-for-fe.evidence: 2026 Meta spec guides converge: 1080x1350 4:5 is the recommended feed size and advertisers report significantly higher CTR on 4:5 vs square/horizontal because mobile users see more of the ad. Our own best static (Muha 'Win Cash') ships at 3:4/2160x2880 and the group-truck at 2:1 — neither is the 4:5 optimum.
static-ad:master-at-4x5-1080x1350-for-fe.counterexamples: Marketplace and some product-grid placements still accept/prefer 1:1. A 3:4 crop (0.75) is close and not disqualifying, just sub-optimal vs 4:5 (0.8).
static-ad:master-at-4x5-1080x1350-for-fe.source: Hootsuite FB ad sizes 2026; TheOptimizer Meta ad sizes 2026; Surfside PPC Meta image specs 2026; adlibrary Meta ad sizes 2026

static-ad:hierarchy-is-the-hook-in-a-sti.claim: In a static, the hook is the visual hierarchy of the first frame, not a line of copy. Within ~500ms the single dominant element must communicate both the offer ('what is this') and the audience ('this is for me') before any text is read. Design one unambiguous focal point; two competing elements is the failure mode.
static-ad:hierarchy-is-the-hook-in-a-sti.evidence: 2026 field guides: with no motion, composition and headline do all the work; effective hooks fire a pattern interrupt AND signal category relevance in the same frame within the ~500ms orienting window. Our 'Win Cash' static works because one offer dominates; product heroes with no hook (hero_caustics) stop the eye but state no offer.
static-ad:hierarchy-is-the-hook-in-a-sti.counterexamples: Retargeting/warm audiences already know the brand, so a product-forward or benefit-stack still with weaker 'audience signalling' can convert on familiarity alone.
static-ad:hierarchy-is-the-hook-in-a-sti.source: adlibrary Meta ad creative best practices 2026; adrio 7 best static formats 2026; ROASPIG scroll-stop hooks 2026

static-ad:contrast-is-the-motion-substit.claim: Replace video's motion with high luminance/colour contrast between a foreground subject and its background — but the contrast must MEAN something (before/after, product-in-use, a reacting face). Decorative contrast underperforms. This is the thumb-stop lever for a still.
static-ad:contrast-is-the-motion-substit.evidence: 2026 guidance: high luminance contrast creates the visual pop that achieves the same attentional effect as motion, and only converts when it 'communicates something'. Corroborated by our house post laws that contrast/acutance above ground truth reads as artefact — contrast must be structural, not cranked.
static-ad:contrast-is-the-motion-substit.counterexamples: Minimalist high-key product statics (clean white, low contrast) still work for premium/marketplace framing where the product and price are the message.
static-ad:contrast-is-the-motion-substit.source: adlibrary Meta ad creative best practices 2026; cross-ref house post_laws sharpening-is-the-tell

static-ad:problem-first-then-product-for.claim: For cold traffic, lead problem-aware and product-second (problem-solution or before-after). Make ONE specific, outcome-tied claim or a concrete social-proof number, not a feature list. Reserve product-forward/benefit-stack statics with visible price+availability for retargeting and marketplace.
static-ad:problem-first-then-product-for.evidence: 2026 DTC analyses: the best cold statics are problem-solution (tell the buyer why to care first); testimonial/benefit-stack are mid/bottom-funnel; specificity wins ('cut 6 hours to 45 minutes' beats 'love it'; '47,000 teams' anchors credibility).
static-ad:problem-first-then-product-for.counterexamples: Impulse/sweepstakes offers (our 'Win $25,000' static) lead with the offer itself, not a problem, and that is correct for that objective; strong brand recognition also lets product-first work cold.
static-ad:problem-first-then-product-for.source: adlibrary best DTC Meta ads 2026; adrio best static formats 2026; gethookd ecommerce FB ads 2026

static-ad:keep-on-image-text-light-and-i.claim: Keep on-image text to roughly one-third of the area or less and place the hook in the centre third; leave ~14% clear at top and ~20-35% clear at bottom for placement UI chrome. Put long-form persuasion in the caption (1-2 sentences, <~125 chars). The 20% rule is gone but lighter text still gets broader delivery.
static-ad:keep-on-image-text-light-and-i.evidence: 2026 spec guides: text ≥1/3 coverage measurably narrows delivery even without a policy rule; Meta recommends ~14% top and 20-35% bottom safe zones for vertical; captions truncate near 125 chars. Our UGC lane already runs zero burned-in text — this law governs the graphic/offer lane instead.
static-ad:keep-on-image-text-light-and-i.counterexamples: Offer/sweepstakes statics (WIN $25,000) intentionally run large-type-dominant and still perform when the type IS the single hook; the guidance is about competing/dense text, not one bold headline.
static-ad:keep-on-image-text-light-and-i.source: WebSearch Meta 4:5 safe-zone/text 2026 (Hootsuite, adlibrary); adlibrary Meta creative best practices 2026

giveaway:prize-specific-and-hero-or-it-r.claim: The prize must be named exactly (brand + model + dollar value), shown as a photoreal object, and be the single largest element. Specificity and brand-plausible scale are the primary legitimacy signal; a vague or implausible prize is the #1 scam tell.
giveaway:prize-specific-and-hero-or-it-r.evidence: RafflePress/Cash App scam-detection guides list 'unrealistic prizes' and 'vague prize descriptions' as top red flags and 'exact prize descriptions aligned with the brand' as the top legitimacy signal. Landing-page best practice puts a clear prize headline + prize image above the fold as one of four required elements. Our own Muha 'Win $25,000 Cash + Dodge Challenger' assets lead with the exact figure and a photoreal car+cash.
giveaway:prize-specific-and-hero-or-it-r.counterexamples: External best practice, not measured on our endpoint. For mystery-box/'surprise' promos a deliberately withheld prize can be the hook — but even those name a floor value.

giveaway:show-the-entry-mechanic-or-its-.claim: A giveaway creative must show the ONE action to enter (on-image line or CTA) and route to a near-zero-friction destination (two-field name+email standard). Without a visible mechanic it drives awareness, not entries; every added required task lowers completion and raises the scam read.
giveaway:show-the-entry-mechanic-or-its-.evidence: KickoffLabs/RafflePress: high-converting giveaway pages use a two-field form and a single clear entry action; giveaway pages convert 25-35% of visitors. Scam guides flag 'excessive entry tasks (download app, refer 10 friends, 20-page survey)' as a red flag. Our Members Raffle Card carries 'LEARN MORE'; the QR raffle-back carries 'Scan In Members App. To Redeem 10 Entries!'.
giveaway:show-the-entry-mechanic-or-its-.counterexamples: External best practice, not measured on our endpoint. Comment-to-enter organic mechanics differ from paid-social lead capture and can invert some rules.
giveaway:show-the-entry-mechanic-or-its-.source: kickofflabs.com giveaway-landing-page-best-practices, rafflepress giveaway-landing-page-examples, cash.app scam guide (2026)

giveaway:disclosure-is-a-trust-signal-no.claim: 'No Purchase Necessary', an age gate where the product is regulated, and an Official-Rules/AMOE reference are legibly present ON the creative or its immediate destination. For chance-based sweeps this is FTC/Meta-required, and its PRESENCE is a positive trust cue that real entrants look for — not merely legal boilerplate to hide.
giveaway:disclosure-is-a-trust-signal-no.evidence: FTC requires no-purchase for chance-based sweeps and clear/conspicuous disclosure of material terms; Meta Promotion Guidelines (updated late 2025) govern all IG/FB promos. Scam guides: 'if there are no Official Rules it's almost always a scam.' Our Muha giveaway spec mandates 'No Purchase Necessary' + 21+ on giveaway assets.
giveaway:disclosure-is-a-trust-signal-no.counterexamples: External/legal best practice, not measured on our endpoint. Skill-contest (non-chance) promos are not required to carry 'No Purchase Necessary'.
giveaway:disclosure-is-a-trust-signal-no.source: viralsweep.com/blog/no-purchase-necessary, auditsocials.com 2026 compliance guide, revup.com Instagram giveaway rules 2026, Muha_Meds.md giveaway spec

giveaway:polished-without-verification-r.claim: Slick graphics ALONE increase the scam read; the offsetting cue is a legitimacy cluster — faithful brand lockup, an 'OFFICIAL ENTRY'/program-name badge, and a verified-identity/rules reference. Reproduce the wordmark from the real file; a garbled logo or misspelling is the strongest visual scam tell.
giveaway:polished-without-verification-r.evidence: Sweeppea/RafflePress: 'fake sweepstakes now come wrapped in polished graphics and real brand logos'; legitimacy signals are verified accounts, consistent branding, and detailed rules; red flags are garbled logos/typos and unverified identity. Our Muha spec bans inventing the Members wordmark and lists specific spellings that 'burned before'.
giveaway:polished-without-verification-r.counterexamples: External best practice, not measured on our endpoint. Verification cues on the creative are weaker than a genuinely verified posting account; the badge helps but the handle is the real proof.
giveaway:polished-without-verification-r.source: sweeppea.com trust-center, rafflepress how-to-spot-a-fake-giveaway, Muha_Meds.md exact-spellings rule

giveaway:urgency-needs-a-dated-deadline-.claim: Urgency must be a concrete deadline or countdown ('Ends Aug 31' / live timer), placed prominently. A dated close lifts entries double digits and reads legitimate; vague or extreme false urgency ('act in 60 minutes!!!') is itself a documented scam signal.
giveaway:urgency-needs-a-dated-deadline-.evidence: RafflePress/KickoffLabs: a visible countdown to the closing deadline 'regularly lifts entries by double digits' and should be visible without scrolling. Scam guides: 'scam notifications create false urgency'; 'real winners have reasonable claim windows — 24-72 hours, not 60 minutes.'
giveaway:urgency-needs-a-dated-deadline-.counterexamples: External best practice, not measured on our endpoint. An always-on evergreen promo has no single deadline and instead uses 'monthly draw' cadence.
giveaway:urgency-needs-a-dated-deadline-.source: rafflepress.com/giveaway-landing-page-examples, kickofflabs.com best-practices, liveabout.com sweepstakes warning signs (2025-26)

commercial:hook-product-and-tension-in-f.claim: In the campaign/brand-video lane, the product and a tension or benefit must be legible in the opening frame and within ~1.5–2s; the hook cannot arrive on a slow build the way it does in the house UGC lane.
commercial:hook-product-and-tension-in-f.evidence: External 2026 paid-social guidance is unanimous that the first 1.5–3s decide retention (71% decide in the first few seconds; hook + product in the opening frames for direct response). This directly conflicts with house:hook-lands-later-than-the-generic-law (house UGC hooks at median 5.1s) — the conflict is real and scoped: late hooks survive on a talking head, not on a scroll-stopping cut-driven spot.
commercial:hook-product-and-tension-in-f.counterexamples: Brand-building TVC-style films tolerate a 3–5s atmospheric open; the 2s rule is a direct-response paid-social rule, not a film-festival one.

commercial:shot-ladder-establish-detail-.claim: A high-production short spot is built from a repeatable shot ladder — at minimum one establishing/wide, one macro/detail insert, one human reaction close-up, one movement shot — with a macro-to-wide scale transition doing the 'quality proof' that copy would otherwise carry.
commercial:shot-ladder-establish-detail-.evidence: External: ~71% of premium product videos use extreme macro-to-wide scale transitions to prove material density; the repeatable system named is establishing moment + one reaction close-up + one detail insert + one movement shot. Builds on sd25:timed-beats-drive-multi-shot-inside-one-generation and sd25:camera-move-vocabulary-one-primary (one camera move per shot).
commercial:shot-ladder-establish-detail-.counterexamples: 29% of premium product videos hold a consistent medium focal length; and the house UGC lane is deliberately single-shot (house:ugc-lane-is-one-unbroken-take) — the ladder is a campaign-lane law only.

commercial:cut-to-the-track-not-the-cloc.claim: Edit the campaign lane to the music — cuts land on beats at a roughly even ~4.3s average shot length across ~7 shots in 30s — and reserve the strongest hero/beauty shot for immediately before the CTA.
commercial:cut-to-the-track-not-the-cloc.evidence: External 2026 editing guidance: 'each beat triggers a motion / a cut', premium pacing is slow prep resolving into the hero. Matches the repo's OWN measured campaign rhythm in house:campaign-lane-cuts-every-4-3s (GOLDEN-HOUR-ANNOUNCE, 7 shots, 4.27s ASL) — this law generalizes that single measured point with the external craft rationale.
commercial:cut-to-the-track-not-the-cloc.counterexamples: House measurement is effectively n=2 (one piece in two ratios); ASL is a guide, not a metronome — a deliberate long hold on the hero is allowed and often wanted.

commercial:legible-with-sound-off-captio.claim: The campaign lane must read fully with sound off — visual story plus burned-in captions — which is the exact INVERSE of the house UGC rule that bans on-screen text; captions are structural in the campaign lane and forbidden in the UGC lane.
commercial:legible-with-sound-off-captio.evidence: External: 75%+ of mobile video is watched muted; TikTok captions lift recall ~58% and brand affinity ~95%. This explicitly contradicts house:no-on-screen-text-in-the-ugc-lane — recording the conflict is the point: the two lanes have opposite caption rules and must not be conflated.
commercial:legible-with-sound-off-captio.counterexamples: A caption that duplicates clear VO on an already-legible visual adds clutter; captions serve comprehension, not decoration. Feed placements with strong autoplay-sound contexts weaken the effect.

commercial:one-graded-look-neutralize-th.claim: Deliver a single saturated, higher-contrast graded look across every shot; first neutralize the per-back-end global colour cast, then push the grade deliberately — a cast left on, or shots that don't match, is the amateur tell.
commercial:one-graded-look-neutralize-th.evidence: External: color grading is named as the divider between amateur and professional, and ad looks run more saturated/high-contrast than documentary. Builds on Pattern F (--neutralize removes the generated wash) and does NOT duplicate the post_laws, which only cover resolution conform/scaling (lanczos p5) and grain — not the creative grade.
commercial:one-graded-look-neutralize-th.counterexamples: Some brand systems mandate a flat/desaturated look (luxury, clinical); 'saturated high-contrast' is the default DR ad register, not a universal.

commercial:brand-locked-cta-card-and-rea.claim: Close on a brand-locked CTA card in the final 2–4s (logo + one action), and carry product/hero fidelity from real brand art composited into a reserved clean plate rather than from a video model's rendering.
commercial:brand-locked-cta-card-and-rea.evidence: External: the hook-problem-solution-proof-CTA framework ends on an explicit CTA/end card. Repo rules: never leave a surface bare or the model invents marks (golden rule 5); compositing a flat logo/QR onto a reserved area is the allowed exception to never-paste (golden rule 2); video models drift on product fidelity (golden rule 10, sd25 first-frame/reference laws).
commercial:brand-locked-cta-card-and-rea.counterexamples: Pure brand-awareness films sometimes withhold an explicit CTA for a single end logo; and over-designed end cards that add a second action reduce click-through.

packshot:ecommerce-hero-is-255-white-and.claim: A marketplace main/packshot image must be pure white RGB 255,255,255 (not off-white or grey), product filling ~85% of the frame, upright and on-axis, with no added text or props. This is a hard marketplace gate, not a style preference.
packshot:ecommerce-hero-is-255-white-and.evidence: Amazon 2026 requirements: hero image pure white RGB 255,255,255, product fills at least 85% of frame, no text; ≥1000px long side minimum, 1600px+ recommended to enable PDP zoom. Corpus 'NuLumin Generated/White BG Powder' meets the white/on-axis/fill spec across 66 SKUs.
packshot:ecommerce-hero-is-255-white-and.counterexamples: The hero/paid-social lane deliberately breaks this (gradient/dark ground, off-center for copy) — the law is scoped to the e-commerce/marketplace lane only. 255-flat white also removes grounding, so it trades realism for compliance.
packshot:ecommerce-hero-is-255-white-and.source: acquireconvert.com Amazon 2026 guide + soona.co Amazon image specs, 2026-08

packshot:key-45-fill-50-70-percent-oppos.claim: Model product form with a key at ~45° to one side and a fill/bounce at ~45° opposite at 50–70% of key intensity. The resulting lit-side/shadow-side gradient is what separates premium from the flat frontal look; specify a light direction, do not ask for 'good lighting'.
packshot:key-45-fill-50-70-percent-oppos.evidence: Squareshot and multiple 2026 studio guides converge on 45° key + opposite fill at 50–70% of key. Corroborated by the repo's own video-lighting instinct in house_laws (shadow side keeps texture, does not lift). Amateur diagnosis: flat, shadowless, evenly-blown frames.
packshot:key-45-fill-50-70-percent-oppos.counterexamples: Small hard-lit jewelry/metal is a deliberate exception (hard light for sparkle). Light-tent/shadowless setups intentionally violate this for tiny reflective parts.

packshot:negative-fill-defines-glossy-an.claim: For glass, gloss and metal, do not try to remove reflections — make them one clean intentional shape by diffusing the key large, and place a black flag/card close to the product opposite the key. Negative fill draws the crisp dark edge; without it glass reads milky and washed out.
packshot:negative-fill-defines-glossy-an.evidence: Multiple 2026 glass-bottle guides (Outshinery, prophotostudio, Amateur Photographer): soft broad key at 45° + fill + rim + a black flag on the far side; 'without negative fill, glass bottles look milky and washed out.' The corpus vials (Vial Library / White BG Powder) are clean but read slightly milky/flat at the edges — the visible symptom of missing negative fill.
packshot:negative-fill-defines-glossy-an.counterexamples: Pure-white e-commerce backgrounds fight negative fill (the white wraps and fills the shadow side back in); the edge-definition trick shows best on gradient/dark hero grounds.

packshot:legibility-outranks-drama-and-a.claim: In the e-commerce lane, correct legible label type beats lighting drama for conversion, and generated packshots reliably melt/garble small label text. Turn the product so the primary name faces the key, keep it hotspot-free, and compose fine ingredient/legal type out of the hero read (or composite it back on a reserved clean panel) rather than shipping garbled type.
packshot:legibility-outranks-drama-and-a.evidence: The Dialed_Moods Blue-Glacier can render shows the failure directly: 'YOUR FULL POTE…' truncated and ingredient lines garbled while the big DIALED lockup reads fine — exactly the small-type melt CLAUDE.md rule 5 warns about for Gemini. Amazon guidance: secondary close-ups exist specifically to carry detail the main image can't.
packshot:legibility-outranks-drama-and-a.counterexamples: gpt-image-2 is documented in CLAUDE.md rule 5 to set small lowercase type accurately (DIALED/HEALTH ECG lockup, 4/4 clean) — so the melt is back-end-specific, not universal. Regulated categories may legally require the fine print visible, forcing a composite rather than a crop.
packshot:legibility-outranks-drama-and-a.source: corpus Dialed_Moods/Blue-Glacier.png + CLAUDE.md rule 5 + Amazon secondary-image guidance, 2026-08

packshot:ground-it-or-a-hard-cutout-halo.claim: Anchor the product with a consistent contact shadow or a soft mirror reflection, or commit to a deliberate soft-falloff float. A hard-edged cutout floating in white with a fringe/halo is the loudest composited/generated tell and reads as amateur regardless of how good the product looks.
packshot:ground-it-or-a-hard-cutout-halo.evidence: 2026 packshot guides: natural drop shadow or mirror reflection added in-camera on a reflective surface or in post is a defining premium trait. Corpus hero/white-BG vials use only a faint reflection; the cleanest reads are the ones with a visible soft contact reflection under the base.
packshot:ground-it-or-a-hard-cutout-halo.counterexamples: Some marketplaces prefer a shadowless float for the main image, and a deliberate clean float with soft edge falloff is legitimate — the failure is specifically the HARD-edged halo, not the absence of a shadow.
